units.title: 初三语法：晚班公共汽车旁的咖啡馆

materials.title: Late Bus Cafe
materials.text:
Last winter, my father and I missed the last direct bus home after visiting my aunt. The station worker ____1____ (TELL) us that another bus would come in an hour, but it would take a longer route. We decided ____2____ (WAIT) rather than ask my aunt to drive through the rain.

A café beside the station was still open. The owner, ____3____ recognised my father from his school days, invited us inside. We bought tea and sat near a window. I could see the stop ____4____ the bus would collect us.

While my father ____5____ (TALK) to the owner, I looked at some old photographs on the wall. One showed the café before a large station building ____6____ (BUILD) beside it. The street had changed, but the same round sign hung above the door.

After ____7____ (FINISH) our tea, we checked the time again. The rain was ____8____ (LIGHT) than before, so waiting outside was no longer unpleasant. The owner gave us a paper bag with two small cakes for the journey.

We thanked her and kept the bag ____9____ (CARE) away from the wet umbrella. When the bus arrived, my father said that missing the first one had given ____10____ (WE) an unexpected hour in a place he had almost forgotten.

decide to do不定式。
逗号非限制定从指owner，who。

father单数过去交谈可进行或一般过去。
单数building被建，可过去或过去完成被动。
After介词后finishing。

修饰kept away动作用carefully。

units.title: 初三语法：没有获奖的风筝

materials.title: Kite Without Prize
materials.text:
Our town held a kite day in the park last spring. My brother ____1____ (SPEND) two evenings painting a bird on his kite. He hoped ____2____ (WIN) the prize for the most interesting design, although he had never entered before.

The morning was brighter ____3____ we had expected, and many families arrived early. A volunteer ____4____ was checking the entries asked my brother to write his name on a small card. I carried the spare paper while he waited.

His kite did not win. At first, he wanted to put it straight back in the bag. Then a younger child stopped ____5____ (LOOK) at the painted bird. She asked how he had made the wings appear different from each other.

My brother explained the colours ____6____ (PATIENT), and her father took a photograph after asking him. For the first time that morning, he talked about the work without mentioning the prize.

Before ____7____ (LEAVE), we read the judges' comments. One said that the design showed an ____8____ (USUAL) use of colour. My brother kept that note beside his drawing plan. The prize had gone to someone else, but ____9____ (HE) work had still given people something to notice. Next year, he plans to bring a new kite and keep this one ____10____ a reminder of his first entry.

questions.explanation: last spring过去spent。

units.title: 初三语法：写给未来读者的时间盒

materials.title: Time Capsule Reader
materials.text:
Our class prepared a time capsule before moving to a new school building. The teacher ____1____ (ASK) each group to choose one object and write an explanation for a future reader. We were not allowed ____2____ (PUT) food or batteries inside.

My group chose a paper lunch card ____3____ had been used in the old dining room. We all knew what it was, so our first note simply said, “This is our lunch card.” The teacher asked whether someone opening the box in twenty years would understand ____4____ it had worked.

We added a description of the weekly menu and the way students showed the card at the counter. After ____5____ (READ) the new note, another group could explain the system back to us. That helped us see which details were clear.

The capsule ____6____ (CLOSE) at a short ceremony on Friday. Each group received a copy of the contents list. We put ____7____ (WE) copy in the class album rather than sealing every record inside the box.

I had thought that choosing an old object was ____8____ (IMPORTANT) than explaining it. Now I understood that both mattered. We listened ____9____ (QUIET) while the teacher described where the capsule would be stored. The box was for the future, but making it helped us notice the ordinary things ____10____ we usually took for granted.

questions.explanation: 过去asked谓语。
be allowed to do不定式。
card作had been used主语，which/that。
understand how it worked询运作方式；what不能接完整worked句。

questions.explanation: 修饰listened用标准-ly副词quietly。

units.title: 初三语法：果园采摘后的两种数量

materials.title: Orchard Picking Record
materials.text:
Our class helped at a small orchard during its open day. Before we began, the owner ____1____ (EXPLAIN) which trees were ready for picking. She asked us ____2____ (KEEP) fruit from different rows in separate boxes.

A student ____3____ had visited before showed me the labels. Each one carried a row number, not a promise that every apple in the row would look exactly the same. Some fruit was smaller ____4____ the rest but still suitable for the uses the owner had planned.

While we ____5____ (WORK), another group weighed the filled boxes. We recorded both the number of boxes and the total weight. The owner said that the two figures answered different questions and should not be mixed together.

After ____6____ (COLLECT) the labels, we checked them against our notes. One box ____7____ (PLACE) beside the wrong row number. We moved the label only after asking the student who had filled it.

At lunch, the owner thanked ____8____ (WE) for checking rather than guessing. The record would help her decide ____9____ to prepare for the next day's visitors. We left the orchard ____10____ (TIRE) but pleased that our notes could still be useful after the fruit had been carried away.

units.title: 初三语法：车站志愿者的小图卡

materials.title: Station Direction Cards
materials.text:
During the autumn holiday, I helped at an information desk in the railway station. On the first morning, a staff member ____1____ (GIVE) us a set of small cards showing common places in the building. They were meant ____2____ (HELP) visitors explain what they were looking for.

A passenger ____3____ spoke very little English pointed to the picture of a lift. I showed him the route on a simple station plan. He then pointed to a second picture, and I realised that he also wanted the ticket office.

I did not speak ____4____ (LOUD) just because he had not understood my first sentence. The staff member had explained that volume and language were different problems. I used shorter phrases and checked ____5____ he wanted to go first.

After ____6____ (WATCH) a few conversations, I understood why the cards were kept in the same order. Familiar positions helped volunteers find the right picture ____7____ (QUICK). The cards supported conversation rather than replacing it completely.

At the end of the shift, we put them back in ____8____ (THEY) case. A torn card ____9____ (REPLACE) before the next group arrived. I had expected the job to be mainly about giving answers, but it was just as much about understanding ____10____ question a visitor was trying to ask.

questions.explanation: 修饰find用标准quickly，显式限定-ly不否定其他语境平义quick。

units.title: 初三语法：行李箱里多出的一件雨衣

materials.title: Raincoat In Suitcase
materials.text:
When we unpacked after a school trip, I found a red raincoat in my suitcase. I had taken a blue one from home, so I knew the red coat ____1____ (BELONG) to someone else. My mother asked me ____2____ (CHECK) the pockets for a name card without removing anything.

There was a paper ticket inside, but no name. The ticket showed the museum ____3____ our class had visited that week. It helped explain how the coat might have come into my bag, but it did not identify its owner.

I sent a message to the teacher ____4____ had organised the trip. She asked the class whether anyone was missing a raincoat and requested a description. One student replied that her coat had a small repair ____5____ the left sleeve.

After ____6____ (LOOK) carefully, I found the repair. The teacher arranged for us to bring the coat to school the next morning. Its owner was ____7____ (HAPPY) to see it than I had expected, because it had been a present from her older sister.

We both checked ____8____ (WE) bags before going home. The coats were different colours, but they had been folded beside each other at the museum. A simple mistake could happen ____9____ (EASY) when everyone was packing in a hurry. I was glad ____10____ (RETURN) something that meant more to its owner than I had first understood.

units.title: 初三语法：生日诗里的熟悉表达

materials.title: Birthday Poem Language
materials.text:
For my grandmother's birthday, I wanted to read a short poem in the language she had spoken as a child. I could pronounce some words, but I ____1____ (NOT/UNDERSTAND) every line. My uncle offered ____2____ (HELP) me practise.

We began with the phrases ____3____ appeared more than once. He explained their meanings and asked me to say them in an ordinary voice before trying to sound like a performer. This made the poem feel ____4____ (CLOSE) than it had when I had only copied the sounds.

While we ____5____ (PRACTISE), my grandmother came into the room unexpectedly. I tried to hide the page, but she smiled and said she recognised the opening. The surprise was no longer secret, yet she stayed to tell us why she liked that poem.

After ____6____ (HEAR) her explanation, I changed the way I read one line. I was not simply repeating a correct sound. I knew ____7____ that line mattered to the person who would hear it.

On the day, I still made a small mistake, but I continued ____8____ (READ) rather than stopping completely. My grandmother thanked ____9____ (WE) both. She said that hearing the poem had brought back a memory ____10____ she had not thought about for years.

units.title: 初三语法：关门图书馆外的小狗

materials.title: Dog At Closed Library
materials.text:
On my way home from school, I noticed a dog waiting outside the library. The building ____1____ (CLOSE) for repairs that week, and no one was at the usual desk. I did not know ____2____ the dog was waiting for.

A neighbour ____3____ often walked past the library stopped beside me. She recognised the dog and phoned its owner. The owner said that it had followed the route he usually took on Tuesday afternoons, even though he had gone somewhere else that day.

We waited ____4____ (PATIENT) at a distance while the neighbour spoke to him. She asked me ____5____ (STAY) with her until he arrived, rather than trying to take the dog home myself. I sent a message to my parent explaining the delay.

After ____6____ (THANK) us, the owner put the dog's lead on and checked the name tag. I had expected him to be angry, but he was mainly ____7____ (RELIEF) to find it. He explained that familiar routes could become a habit.

The library opened again a week later. When I saw the owner there, he told me the dog was waiting at home with ____8____ (HE) sister. units.title: 初三完形：队服上没有印错的名字

materials.title: Name On Team Shirt
materials.text:
When a new student joined our running club, I offered to order her team shirt. Her name was Rina, but I had only heard it once in a noisy room. I almost typed a ____1____ that looked familiar to me instead of checking what she had said.

The club leader noticed my unfinished form and asked whether I was certain. I felt embarrassed. I thought asking again would show that I had not listened, ____2____ she said that guessing would create a different problem. A printed name would stay on the shirt long after that short conversation.

I asked Rina to write her name for me. She did so ____3____ and thanked me for checking. She explained that people sometimes changed the spelling to match a name they already knew. I realised that my familiar version would not be a small improvement; it would be a ____4____ about her identity.

We checked the size as well. ____5____ of choosing what I thought looked right, I showed her the size guide and asked her preference. She wanted a shirt large enough to wear over another top in cold weather.

When the shirts arrived, Rina opened hers and smiled. The club leader asked me ____6____ I had learned from the order. I said that a helpful action could still include a question. Asking did not have to mean I cared less or knew ____7____. It could mean that the other person's answer had more ____8____ than my first assumption.

Rina wore the shirt at our next meeting. I could see her name clearly ____9____ the back. It was a small piece of information, but one that we had ____10____ rather than invented.

units.title: 初三完形：接力练习里的交接

materials.title: Relay Practice Partner
materials.text:
At the start of the term, our coach asked us to practise a short relay in pairs. I was pleased to ____1____ my fastest friend. I expected that having a quick partner would make every part of the task easy.

The first attempt did not go well. I began running before she was ready to pass the baton, and she had to call me back. I wanted to try again immediately, but the coach asked us to ____2____ what had happened first. Speed did not explain the whole problem.

My friend said she could not tell when I was going to move. I had been looking ahead instead of watching for our agreed signal. We practised the exchange while standing still, then added a few slow steps. It felt less exciting, ____3____ it made the order clearer.

On the next run, I waited for the signal. The exchange was smoother, even though neither of us was moving at full speed. I began to ____4____ why the coach had separated the small action from the complete race.

A younger pair nearby were struggling with the same point. My friend asked whether we could show them the practice we had used. I was surprised to find myself offering ____5____ rather than simply comparing times. We demonstrated the signal and then let them try it in their own way.

By the end of the lesson, I still liked running fast. I also knew that a quick result could depend ____6____ a careful routine between two people. We had improved not by finding a faster partner but by making our actions more ____7____.

The coach did not announce a winning pair that afternoon. She asked each group to explain one change it had made. I described the moment ____8____ I had learned to wait. It was a small part of a relay, yet it had made a real ____9____ to how we worked together. My friend nodded, and we put the baton back ____10____ the next pair could use it.

units.title: 初三完形：窗边那幅未完成的速写

materials.title: Window Sketch Return
materials.text:
Our art class visited the town square to practise quick sketches. The teacher gave us twenty minutes and asked us to choose one small part of the scene. I chose a café window filled with plants because it looked ____1____ enough to finish quickly.

After ten minutes, I had drawn only the frame. I kept rubbing out lines because they were not exactly like the window. A classmate sat beside me and asked what I wanted the sketch to ____2____. I said I wanted it to look correct.

She pointed to a reflection moving across the glass. If I waited for every detail to stay the same, I might never begin the plants. I started drawing the larger shapes ____3____ trying to copy every leaf. The page became less exact in some ways and more like my experience of looking at the window.

When the teacher called us back, the sketch was unfinished. I wanted to put it away before anyone saw it. The teacher asked me to ____4____ one decision I had made. I showed her where I had changed the plant shapes after noticing the reflection.

She did not tell me that every line was perfect. She said the page could help me decide what to ____5____ next. A quick study was allowed to contain evidence of a choice, a question or a change of mind.

The following week, I returned to the square on my own with permission from my family. The café owner ____6____ me sitting outside and said the plants had grown since the class visit. I made a second sketch beside the first, using the same notebook.

Comparing them later, I could see changes in both the window and my way of looking. Finishing one perfect picture was not the only possible ____7____ of the visits. The two pages gave me something to compare. I kept them ____8____ rather than replacing the early one with the later one. The unfinished sketch had become ____9____ as a record of a beginning. It reminded me that practice could be visible ____10____ a page, not just hidden behind a final result.

units.title: 初三完形：共享书架里的一盒游戏

materials.title: Shared Shelf Game
materials.text:
Our apartment building has a small shelf where neighbours can leave books and simple games for others to borrow. One evening, I found a board game that I remembered from childhood. The box looked complete, but there was no list of the ____1____ inside.

I took it home and set it out with my younger sister. Halfway through, we discovered that several cards were missing. She thought we had misunderstood the rules. I wanted to invent new cards quickly so that we could ____2____, but my father suggested checking whether the missing pieces affected the game first.

She apologised and found the missing cards in a drawer. Her family had used them separately and forgotten to return them. Once the cards were back, the game made ____4____ to my sister. The difficulty had not come from her failure to understand.

Before putting it on the shared shelf again, we checked the contents ____5____ the list. We also added a small card asking future borrowers to report any missing parts. This would not guarantee that nothing was ever lost, ____6____ it gave the next person a way to explain a problem.

My sister asked why we had kept the first note after the cards were found. I said it showed what had happened, though we also wrote that the issue had been ____7____. A record needed an ending as well as a complaint. We did not want the next borrower to believe the cards were ____8____ missing.

The game went back on the shelf with its pieces together. Sharing it meant more than leaving a colourful box in a public place. It also meant passing ____9____ enough information for someone else to use it. My sister chose it again the following weekend, this time with more ____10____.
